title: Why paying an advisor a percent of assets every year is questionable
summary: The speaker, who worked on Wall Street for 25 years, says a yearly fee as a percent of assets makes no sense. You do not pay an estate attorney a percent of your estate or a plumber a percent of your house. He says he is building a tool for do-it-yourself option traders.

steps.caption: Many possible paths of a portfolio over time. A fee is charged on the whole value every year, in every path.
Each blue path is one possible outcome. A percent fee grows as the portfolio grows, even if the work does not.
The median path. A yearly percent fee compounds against you over the same years that returns compound for you.
In a drawdown the fee is still charged. You pay for the service, not for the result.
The speaker's view: pay for a service at a fixed price, like an attorney or a plumber.

takeaways: A fee as a percent of assets is charged every year on the whole portfolio.
The speaker compares it to paying a plumber a percent of your house value.
Do-it-yourself investors can avoid the fee if they manage their own risk.
caveats: The speaker promotes a tool he is building; it is unverified here.
The chart shows generic portfolio paths, not a fee calculation from the video.
